newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon set to transfer Rwanda genocide suspects.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon set to transfer Rwanda genocide suspects.

text.p: Cameroon is ready to hand over four suspects to the U.N. tribunal on Rwanda's genocide following the signing of a decree for their transfer by President Paul Biya, a senior Cameroon official said on Monday.
"The president signed the decree for the transfer of the four Rwandans on January 6, 1997," justice ministry's director of judicial affairs, Christian Mballe, told Reuters.
"We have informed the Interrnational Crminal Tribunal on Rwanda in Arusha and are waiting for arrangements to be made for this transfer," he added.
Cameroon is holding 12 Rwandans wanted for their role for the 1994 massacre in Rwanda of some 800,000 minority Tutsis and their Hutu sympathisers by hardliners of the majority Hutu.
For now the U.N. Tribunal based in Arusha, Tanzania, only wants prime suspect Colonel Theoneste Bagosora, a top official of the defence ministry during the massacres, and three others.
The other three are Ferdinand Nahimana, Anatole Nsengiyumva amd Andre Ntagerura.

Nahimana was a director and senior administrative officer of Radio television Mille Collines, which in broadcasts from Kigali incited Hutus to slaughter Tutsis during the three-month genocide. Nsengiyumva is a former chief of military intelligence and Ntagerura a former minister of transport and communications.
Cameroon arrested all 12 suspects last March.
Bagosora was initially sought by Rwanda itself and and by Belgium in connection with the killing of 10 Belgian U.N. peacekeepers at the start of the massacres in April 1994.

Cameroon courts ruled in June that in international law the Arusha tribunal outweighs national courts and approved the handover of all 12 suspects for trial. The tribunal asked for the first four while it gathered more information on the others.
But the handover of the suspects has been held up by Cameroon Biya who has sole political authority to decree their transfer, Cameroon officials said.

The Arusha tribunal's registrar, Andronico Adede, left Yaounde on October 4 in frustration after spending nearly a week there trying to arrange the transfer. He never managed to have a promised meeting with Biya.
